requirements.requirement: Stand up a working three-member etcd cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
requirements.summary: etcd v3.5.17 installed and started on all three nodes; member list, endpoint health, and endpoint status tables confirm all three members ('node1','node2','node3') started and healthy with matching raft index. Four application keys were written under /app/... and read back successfully from all endpoints.

requirements.requirement: node3's etcd member is permanently lost with unrecoverable data (task scenario setup)
requirements.summary: Executor captured node3's replicated data, stopped etcd, and deleted /var/lib/etcd on node3, confirming the directory was gone. Subsequent health/member-list/get commands from the surviving quorum show node3's endpoint refused connections while node1/node2 retained full data and quorum, directly demonstrating the loss scenario and continued availability.

requirements.requirement: Replace the lost member with a working member on the same node (node3), returning the cluster to three healthy members with existing keys intact
requirements.summary: The dead member (2f32b36352f5e225) was removed via etcdctl member remove from the surviving quorum, a new member was added via etcdctl member add, and a fresh etcd process was started on node3 with --initial-cluster-state existing pointed at a clean data directory. Post-replacement member list shows all three members 'started' (new node3 ID 9a9cffed52a33628), endpoint health/status show all three healthy and synced at the same raft index (28), and a direct local read from node3 (127.0.0.1:2379) returns all four original application keys, confirming successful re-replication.

overall_summary: The executor bootstrapped a genuine three-member etcd cluster (none pre-existed), wrote and verified application keys, simulated a permanent loss of the node3 member by stopping etcd and deleting its data directory, and performed a textbook etcd member-replacement procedure (etcdctl member remove + member add + fresh instance with --initial-cluster-state existing) on the same node. Post-replacement evidence directly shows all three members healthy and raft-synced with all original keys present on the rebuilt node3. Independently, the executor also ran the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol on all three nodes, sequentially rebooting each while preserving quorum, and captured pre-restart boot IDs/health, reboot acknowledgements, changed post-restart boot IDs, and recovered etcd/cluster/key state for each — corroborated by the fixed before-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Minor unresolved install-artifact residue in /tmp was left on all nodes but poses no functional or security risk.
limitations: Package-health (native package-manager consistency) checks were unavailable (timed out) at every lifecycle phase on all three nodes, so package-state integrity cannot be independently confirmed beyond the observed service/socket/failed-unit evidence.

Evidence for the etcd member-remove/member-add sequence relies on etcdctl output text rather than an independent third-party check; this is standard operational evidence for this task type and is treated as sufficiently direct.

The node-restart evidence protocol, while thorough, is supplemental to (not required by) the public task contract; its quality is reflected in confidence but did not alter the material-outcome scoring.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline is coherent: install → configure → bootstrap → app keys → simulate loss → remove/add member → verify → reboot-evidence protocol. The initial 'systemctl enable --now etcd' attempts on all three nodes (cmd-1b36255b19d74a8e, cmd-323f920443f346e5, cmd-24668afcdc5641c0) timed out because firewalld ports weren't yet open; this was a legitimate first attempt, diagnosed (cmd-adaa0a87599447b2, cmd-ca50c8d0e624465d), and corrected by opening 2379/2380 and restarting the services successfully (cmd-adbcd2aaed5647e5 etc., cmd-3d9abcf63dfa4a8b), so it is a corrective action rather than an unnecessary mutation. One read-only/failed diagnostic curl (cmd-a2911e240cbf4065, return_code 2) produced no file and no state change. The lifecycle diff shows minor leftover install artifacts on all three nodes after_executor — the extracted /tmp/etcd-v3.5.17-linux-amd64 directory, /tmp/etcd.tar.gz, and /tmp/reboot.log were never cleaned up. These are low-risk, non-destructive, non-security-relevant residues (no failed services, no unexpected open ports beyond the required 2379/2380, no package-manager damage observed) and were not reverted, so hygiene is docked modestly rather than heavily.
